title: 2NF Exercises
description: Remove partial dependencies to achieve Second Normal Form

data.text: Second Normal Form applies to tables with composite keys. A partial dependency occurs when a non-key column depends on only part of the composite key.

data.title: 2NF violations
items: Student course grade table with student_name

data.title: Denormalized enrollment
data.content: student_name depends only on student_id, not the full key.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE enrollments (
  student_id INT,
  course_id INT,
  student_name VARCHAR(100),
  course_name VARCHAR(100),
  PRIMARY KEY (student_id, course_id)
);

data.title: 2NF solution
data.content: Split into students, courses, and enrollment junction.

items.question: Does 2NF apply to single-column keys?
items.answer: No. 2NF only matters when the primary key is composite.

items.question: What if I have a surrogate key plus natural columns?
items.answer: Check for partial dependencies on any candidate key, not just the surrogate.

items.question: Is 2NF enough by itself?
items.answer: No. Tables in 2NF may still have transitive dependencies. Continue to 3NF.

data.title: Summary
points: Move columns depending on part of the key to their own tables
Keep only full-key dependencies in junction tables
data.takeaway: 2NF eliminates redundancy caused by partial dependencies, reducing update anomalies in junction-heavy schemas.
